mainEntity.name: How long does it take to recemented a dental crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: The recementation procedure itself is typically completed within a single appointment and usually takes between 30 and 60 minutes, depending on the clinical assessment required. Your dentist will first examine the crown and tooth, take any necessary X-rays, and then clean and reattach the crown if appropriate. In most cases, the process is straightforward and comfortable, though your dentist will advise on what to expect based on your individual situation.

mainEntity.name: Is recementation of a crown painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recementation is generally not a painful procedure. If the exposed tooth is sensitive, your dentist may use a local anaesthetic to ensure your comfort. The cleaning and reattachment process itself involves minimal discomfort for most patients. You may notice some sensitivity in the days following the appointment, particularly if the tooth had been exposed for a period of time, but this usually settles as the area stabilises.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to recemented a dental crown in London?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of recementation varies depending on the dental practice, the complexity of the appointment, and whether additional investigations such as X-rays are required. It is generally less costly than having a new crown made. Your dental practice will be able to provide a treatment cost following assessment. It is always advisable to contact the practice directly for up-to-date pricing information specific to your clinical needs.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I leave a loose crown and do not get it treated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Leaving a loose or fallen crown unaddressed can lead to further complications. Without the protection of the crown, the underlying tooth is more vulnerable to decay, sensitivity, and structural damage. In some cases, bacteria can work their way under a loose crown, causing decay to progress beneath it. Early professional attention may support simpler treatment outcomes compared to delaying care, though this will depend on individual clinical circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Can a crown be recemented multiple times?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some situations, a crown may be recemented more than once over its lifespan. However, if a crown requires repeated recementation over a short period, this may indicate an underlying issue — such as an ill-fitting crown, ongoing decay, or bruxism — that needs to be addressed. Your dentist will advise on whether repeated recementation is clinically appropriate or whether a new restoration may be a more suitable long-term solution.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my crown is loose before it falls out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some patients notice early warning signs that a crown may be loosening. These can include a slight rocking or movement sensation when biting, a change in how the crown feels in the mouth, increased sensitivity to temperature or pressure, or an unusual taste around the affected tooth. If you notice any of these signs, it is advisable to contact your dentist to have the crown checked, even if it has not yet come off completely.
